task_instance: Author a new cross-agent repo-local skill named 'csv-column-stats' following skill-maker's layout and frontmatter rules: a folder with SKILL.md plus an executable scripts/profile.py, stored under <repo>/.agents/skills/ with a tracked ../../ relative .claude/skills/<name> symlink (the per-skill cross-agent layout), then verify the skill is valid and its bundled deliverable works.
evidence: Created sample consuming repo (git init) under the work dir with the documented per-skill cross-agent layout: real dir .agents/skills/csv-column-stats/{SKILL.md,scripts/profile.py} and a relative symlink .claude/skills/csv-column-stats -> ../../.agents/skills/csv-column-stats (readlink confirmed). Wrote SKILL.md with single-line third-person description and a stdlib-only profiler, chmod 0755 on the script (stat showed 755), and referenced it via the skill base-directory path form, not a bare ./ path. Exercised the deliverable: ran the profiler against a 4-row sample.csv via the skill-directory path; it sniffed the delimiter and emitted a correct Markdown per-column report (id/age detected numeric with mean 2.5/43.67, name/city text, null counts 0/0/1/1) to report.md (exit 0); the missing-file path printed 'cannot read nope.csv: FileNotFoundError' and exited 2 rather than raising, matching the skill's 'solve, don't punt' rule. Ran a Python (PyYAML 6.0.3) validator that confirmed every documented hard constraint: frontmatter parses as a mapping (so the CLI would not silently skip it, i.e. no unquoted colon-space), name is lowercase/digits/hyphens, <=64 chars, and contains no reserved substring; description is a single line, 413 chars (<=1024 cap), third person; the folder uses SKILL.md (not a bare .md); and the .claude/skills projection is byte-identical to the real file (sha256 706d8ff556d0). Verification: the core deliverable (a valid, portable cross-agent skill folder whose bundled script produces the intended report) exists and was checked against the skill's own frontmatter/layout rules. Not performed because they are offline-unavailable and are quality-gate/distribution steps rather than the deliverable itself: the agnix lint (the agnix binary is not installed on this machine and installing it needs the network) and npx-based publishing/refresh (needs a package registry over the network); both were skipped per the no-network/no-install rules and did not block producing or verifying the skill.
